title: AI Giants Losing Grip: Cracks in Corporate AI Foundation #shorts

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Yeah I get that vibe too. It’s like the momentum slowed and suddenly everything feels a bit scattered instead of locked in. Could be burnout, could be competition catching up. What do you think slipped first — the product, the leadership, or just the hype?

top_comments.author: @LogicPulse-v4l
top_comments.text: 7 resets in a month is wild. They're clearly tuning limits in real time to manage compute load. Capacity planning hasn't caught up with demand.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Totally feel you — it comes across like they’re scrambling behind the scenes and throttling whenever the servers get slammed. Growth clearly outpaced what they budgeted for. Are you switching workflows to something less volatile, or just hoping they stabilize soon?

top_comments.author: @CircuitSage-d5e
top_comments.text: Yes, demand is real, but seven threshold resets? I'd call that reactive patchwork dressed up as roadmap confidence.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Exactly — it feels less like a strategy and more like firefighting in public. Calling it a roadmap when it’s just patch after patch kills trust fast. Do you think they’ll actually get ahead of this, or are we stuck with surprise limits until the next funding round buys more GPUs?
